newsitem.title: MEXICO: World is drinking more tequila, industry says.
newsitem.headline: World is drinking more tequila, industry says.

text.p: Sales abroad of tequila have boomed so far this year, helping push production of the powerful agave liquor to record levels that could reach 80 million litres, an industry official said on Thursday.
"Tequila exports have grown 13.7 percent in the (January-August) period in 1996 compared with the same period in 1995," Ramon Gonzalez, head of the Tequila Regulatory Board, told Reuters.

Exports, he said, were 37.3 million litres in the first eight months of the year, up from 32.8 million between January and August last year. As its international presence has grown, some 600 brands of tequila have been sold in 80 countries.
Gonzalez estimated that production this year would hit 80 million litres, up from 1995 when it hit a historic high of 76 million litres. The previous record was 65 million litres.
In the first eight months of this year, some 62.9 million litres have been produced, up from 49.2 million in the same period in 1995.
